name: Dongmin Go
headline: Robotics Software Engineer
profile_affiliation: M.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Chung-Ang University
summary: I am a robotics software engineer focused on reinforcement learning and robot control. I earned my M.S. in Mechanical Engineering from Chung-Ang University, where I conducted research in the Assistive and Rehabilitation Robotics Lab under the supervision of Prof. Giuk Lee.
homepage_interest_statement: My research interests include human-robot interaction, reinforcement learning in simulation, and robot control.
homepage_goal_statement: My goal is to contribute to the development of companion robots that interact naturally and reliably with people in everyday life.
background: Previously, I worked as a wearable robotics software engineer at HUROTICS and as an Equipment Engineer in the Memory Business of Samsung Electronics' Device Solutions (DS) Division, responsible for EUV lithography equipment. I also received my B.S. in Mechanical Engineering from Chung-Ang University.

projects.title: AI Sapiens K1: Humanoid Locomotion Learning
projects.description: Extended my experience with human walking models to humanoid locomotion in Isaac Lab. Compared PPO with off-policy FastSAC across five training seeds per method; FastSAC first reached 95% of each run's peak mean validation episode score in 70% less training time.
details: Ran the Cyclo Lab PPO baseline and adapted FastSAC to the same K1 robot, observations, actions, rewards, and environment settings.
Compared five training seeds per method under a shared 5.5-hour time budget, separating checkpoint selection from held-out testing.

Reduced the time to first observe 95% of each run's peak mean validation episode score by 70.1%: PPO 117.7 min versus FastSAC 35.2 min, averaged across five training seeds. Checkpoints were sampled on a five-minute time grid.
Reduced mean planar velocity tracking RMSE by 22.8% in held-out flat-ground simulation tests under the shared training-time budget.
cv_details: Adapted off-policy FastSAC to the Isaac Lab / Cyclo Lab K1 task; compared against PPO across five seeds per method.
Cut time to first reach 95% of each run's peak mean validation score by 70%: PPO 117.7 min; FastSAC 35.2 min.
Reduced held-out planar velocity RMSE by 23% under a shared 5.5-hour training budget in simulation.

figures.alt: Mean validation episode score of time-selected PPO and FastSAC checkpoints
figures.caption: Validation episode score (mean ± SD across five training seeds). First observed reach of 95% of each run's own peak: PPO 117.7 ± 13.6 min; FastSAC 35.2 ± 8.3 min. Times are computed per seed, then averaged.

figures.alt: Mean validation episode duration of PPO and FastSAC checkpoints
figures.caption: Validation episode duration (mean ± SD across five training seeds). Every checkpoint uses the same 384 first episodes, including failures. Step curves carry forward each seed’s latest evaluated checkpoint; no smoothing or future interpolation.

figures.alt: Held-out planar velocity tracking RMSE for PPO and FastSAC across five training seeds
figures.caption: Held-out planar velocity tracking. Mean RMSE decreased from 0.0995 to 0.0768 m/s (22.8%).

figures.caption: Held-out yaw-rate tracking. Mean RMSE was 0.1066 rad/s for PPO and 0.0989 rad/s for FastSAC.

videos.title: PPO vs. off-policy FastSAC at 15, 70 and 120 min
videos.caption: Training seed 42, a 0.5 m/s forward command, and matched initial poses. The shown policies were selected by validation mean episode score within ±3 min of each stage. The lower lines show five-seed mean validation scores; diamonds mark the shown policies. Curves stop at the actual displayed checkpoint times. Each rollout lasts 13.32 s at 1× speed. The closing Test panel is the separate final-budget evaluation.

validation_milestone.definition: For each training seed: first evaluated grid-selected checkpoint reaching 95% of that run own maximum validation mean episode return among grid-selected checkpoints within 330 min. Use actual checkpoint time; average the five first-reach times. No hold and no interpolated crossing. Video-only extra checkpoints excluded from milestone.
validation_milestone.temporal_resolution: Five-minute selection grid; saved checkpoint times differ from nominal budgets. First observed attainment, no interpolated crossing.

projects.title: H-MEDI Wearable Robot at CES 2025
projects.role: High-Level Control Algorithm Development & Live Demonstration
projects.description: Motion-aware assistance for a rehabilitation-assist wearable robot, from high-level control development and integration to live demonstrations at CES 2025.
details: Developed and integrated motion-state recognition and target assistance-force generation for walking, stopping, and transitions between sitting and standing.
Operated live demonstrations, responded to unexpected on-site situations, and managed the robot and batteries between demonstrations.
